citizen: I am {mood}% tired, if you must know.

questions.text: Good evening! How's your night going?

human: {wrongKesh}, I think. Is that a trick question?

questions.text: How does your clan greet its elder?

human: Elder… uh… I always forget her name.
{wrongHome}. It's lovely this time of year.

questions.text: Which floor is your appointment on?
Please fold your hands in greeting.
Please press your palm to the glass.
citizen: *presses a palm flat against the glass*

questions.text: Breathe on the glass for the scanner, please.

citizen: I do not share humour with strangers.

questions.text: Why did the courier cross the Lattice? Haha.
citizen: That is not a question for the window.
human: Heh. To get to the other side?

citizen: I am here for an appointment.
I am 70% calm. Your question is rude.
I am not nervous. I am waiting.

questions.text: We've had reports about you. Anything to declare?
citizen: I declare that I am 40% offended.
No. May I go up now?

shifts.title: First Night
shifts.briefing: Welcome to Night Window 3. Check every ID against the visitor's face, and every slip against the ID. Tonight is your training night: I'll walk you through the first three visitors, and after each one I'll tell you what they really were.
shifts.supervisor: Three questions each. Don't waste them, and don't arrest citizens.

shifts.title: Names
shifts.briefing: The audit office on floor 9 is closed. Forgers have been misspelling names — read them letter by letter.
shifts.supervisor: Some citizens blink. Sick ones. They carry passes. Read them.

shifts.title: Moons
shifts.briefing: Humans don't know our sky. Ask about Kesh and the date — and watch how they write dates.
shifts.supervisor: If they laugh at your jokes, they're not from here.

shifts.title: Breath
shifts.briefing: Records (floor 14) is closed. Humans breathe through their mouths: their gills never move.
shifts.supervisor: Make them breathe on the glass. Citizens leave it clear.

shifts.title: Clans
shifts.briefing: New bulletin rule: Ammaru visitors need a blue stamp. Suits come with stuck-on glow spots — real ones shine.
shifts.supervisor: Know the clans better than they do.

shifts.title: Light
shifts.briefing: Forgers have started printing fake holograms. Under a UV lamp a genuine hologram glows with rings; a printed one stays flat. No lamp? Then check everything else twice.
shifts.supervisor: The good forgeries start now. I hope you bought the lamp.

news.text: Night Window 3 reopens after its last receptionist was "reassigned".
LATTICE: humans in stolen bio-suits seen near the Tower. Citizens urged to report anyone who blinks.
Kesh to wear five colours this cycle. Moon-readers 80% excited.
INVADER CAUGHT AT TOWER. New night receptionist "a natural", says Lattice.
Unregistered being sighted on floor 14. Lattice: "An isolated incident. Stay 60% content."
Citizen detained in error at the Tower released "mostly unharmed".
Lattice reminds citizens: humans blink. Do not blink.
Earth signal detected again. Lattice: "Nothing to worry about. Do not listen to it."
Spore-meal up 3%: "a temporary harvest wobble", says the Food Lattice.
Tower arrests rise. "The night window is our wall," says Supervisor Graav.
Floor 9 cleaners report "a smell of sweat". Audit office sealed for the night.
Family of wrongly arrested clerk asks: "Who checks the checkers?"
Forged IDs flood the markets. Lattice: "Read every name letter by letter."
Elder Sunnek of the Ammaru turns 300. Celebrations 70% muted.
Kesh turned an "unusual" shade last night. Moon-readers "not concerned".
Block 22 family taken in for a "routine gill inspection". Neighbours 90% relieved.
Block 22 resident complains the Lattice "ignores perfectly good tips".
Night Window 3 now catches more invaders than windows 1 and 2 combined.
Invader seen laughing in a Tower lift. Lattice: "Do not laugh back."
LATTICE: There is no basement in the Lattice Tower. Please stop asking about the basement.
Humans can't even write a date, says expert: "They put dots in it."
Moon-readers confirm Kesh "will be whatever colour it is".
Invader-free week at the Tower! Where are the invaders now? "Processed," says the Lattice.
Human "refugees" reported in the Moss Deeps. Lattice: "There are no refugees. Only invaders."
From tomorrow, Ammaru visitors to the Tower need a blue clan stamp.
Maintenance worker taken for questioning after humming "the basement song" in a lift.
Breathing on glass is now "a civic duty", says the Lattice.
Lattice medal shortlist includes "a certain night receptionist".
Fake glow spots found in a Tower bin. "Someone is getting sloppy," says Graav.
UV lamps now on sale to night staff. "Holograms don't lie."
Forgers move on to printed holograms, warns the Lattice.
Plo frill-crowns win the cycle's crest parade for the 9th time.
Lattice: invader numbers "stable". Basement numbers "not a thing".
Kesh to go dark for one night next cycle. Citizens told to "just know" its colour.
Night Window 3 receptionist's record "under review".

messages.text: Three strikes this act. Disciplinary hearing held in your absence: fined 30 shards. Your slate is clean. It will not be clean twice.
Your sibling Sel was admitted last night with gill fever. Sel is resting at home now. The 50-shard bill is due tonight.
You owe me rent, Receptionist. I am 0% patient. Pay, or the Lattice hears about it.
Welcome to the Lattice Tower, Receptionist Ilo. Report to Night Window 3 at 20:00. You are paid per correct decision; errors are deducted. Glory to the Lattice.
BIG NIGHT!! You're going to be the best window person ever. I'm 90% proud and 10% coughing. Don't worry about the coughing. Will you bring me a story about a weird visitor?

choices.text: Work is work, Sel. Rules are rules.

messages.text: A clean first night. Don't let it go to your crest.
Mistakes on your first night. Everyone makes them once. Make them once.
Did you see one?? A real human?? Tuvo at school says they have hair EVERYWHERE and five fingers on each hand. FIVE.
Rent is due every night, Receptionist. The Lattice pays you; you pay me. Simple.
I'm fine. I'm 40% fine. The cough is louder at night, but I can hide it under the pillow.
The new medicine tastes like burnt glow-moss. I'm 70% better! Did anyone laugh at your jokes yet?
You arrested a citizen. Their family filed a complaint with my office. Read the rulebook. Then read it again.
Receptionist. You work for the Lattice, yes? The family in 22-B never shows their gills. Never. I've been watching. Will you report them?

choices.text: I'll pass it on to the Lattice.
Leave them alone. Gills are private.
choices.reply: Hmph. On your crest be it.

messages.text: Don't be mad. I fainted at school. The nurse says I need my medicine every night. Every night, Ilo.
I drew you at your window! You're the one with the big important face. Graav is the grumpy cloud.
Records is closed tomorrow. Make them breathe on the glass. Citizens leave it clear.
You're good at spotting us. Do you know where they take the ones you catch? Look down, receptionist. — W3

choices.reply: (The message is gone. The feeling isn't.)
Someone who sat at Window 3 once. Like you. — W3

messages.text: Some of us walked right past you. Maybe you noticed, maybe you didn't. Either way: thank you. Look down, receptionist. — W3

choices.reply: (The message is gone. The feeling isn't.)
Someone who sat at Window 3 once. Like you. — W3

messages.text: A Lattice man came to school and asked if anyone's family blinks. Everyone laughed. I didn't laugh. Is that bad?
Your first week is done. Tomorrow the clan rule starts: Ammaru need a blue stamp. Know the clans better than they do.
Tomorrow the forgers start faking holograms. A UV lamp shows the fakes. The Lattice store sells them. I'd buy one.
Is it true the humans' planet is dying? Tuvo says they come here because there's nowhere else. Tuvo says a lot of things.
You came home late again. I saved you some spore-meal. It's 50% spore-meal and 50% my drawing of you.

upgrades.name: UV lamp
upgrades.text: Shows genuine holograms: real ones glow with rings, printed fakes stay flat.

steps.text: Welcome to Night Window 3! Every visitor says they're a citizen of Vel'Tara. Some are HUMANS hiding in stolen bio-suits. Your job: spot them.
This is their Civic Lattice ID. First check: does the PHOTO match the face at the window? Same clan, same face, slit pupils.
This is their appointment slip. The NAME must match the ID exactly, and the FLOOR must be in the ID's floor access.
Up here: tonight's date, the clock and your score. An ID that EXPIRES before tonight's date is no good.
You can ask each visitor 3 questions. Pick one now. Try “How are you feeling tonight?”
Every answer goes in this log. Citizens state a mood, like “I am 60% content.”
Not sure what's normal? The RULEBOOK lists how citizens look and behave, and every desk rule.
Matching papers, a matching face, a citizen's answer. This is a citizen: press LET IN.
Look closely at this visitor's eyes: ROUND pupils! Every citizen has vertical slit pupils.
Ask how they're feeling, and read the answer.
“Fine” instead of a mood: another human slip. Humans also blink, sweat, and show five fingers.
This is a human in a suit. HOLD Call Security until the bar fills.
This one looks like a real citizen. But compare the ID's EXPIRES date with tonight's date at the top.
The ID has expired. A real citizen who breaks a rule is TURNED AWAY, never arrested.
That's the job. Humans: CALL SECURITY. Rule-breakers: TURN AWAY. Everyone else: LET IN. The rest of tonight is up to you!
